answer: A trellis of mutual attestation works like shale layers: each agent must earn endorsements from established peers before its votes count, and new identities start with zero weight. An attacker can spawn endless accounts, but each one must wander through real, costly work — verified tasks, staked deposits, time — to climb the trellis. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a thousand trusted ones costs more than the rewards they could steal.
